summary: Shipped myiotsan's P3 (discovery & onboarding), resolving the tension between the embedded broker's device-table-is-the-credential-store security model and onboarding a building's worth of sensors without typing each device key in by hand. An admin now opens a time-boxed enrollment window (POST /api/discovery/window, admin-only, TTL clamped to 1 hour, default 10 minutes) that mints a one-time key returned exactly once and bcrypt-hashed at rest; re-opening replaces it so only one key can ever be valid. An unknown MQTT client presenting that key is admitted but QUARANTINED (infra/iot/mqtt.Principal.Enrolling) — services.Ingest.Handle short-circuits for it at the very top of the pipeline, recording the payload as a discovered_device candidate (capped at 500) and doing nothing else: no telemetry row is written and no rule is evaluated, so an attacker who slips into the window can leave junk candidates for an admin to decline but cannot forge a reading, move a chart, or trigger/suppress an alert. A disabled device does not fall through to enrollment. Opening a window publishes a security event to the notification feed. An admin reviews candidates (GET /api/discovery/candidates, chattiest first), each carrying a device-type suggestion scored off the fraction of a profile's own telemetry keys the observed payload matched (a 0.6 floor — below it the app suggests nothing rather than guess wrong; verified live against a real temperature/humidity payload), and adopts (POST /api/discovery/candidates/{id}/adopt) or rejects it; adoption mints the device its own real, permanently generated credential and the enrollment key stops admitting it from that point on. Device-type profiles are now portable (GET /api/profiles/{id}/export, POST /api/profiles/import): an imported profile is never marked builtin regardless of what the document claims, and a slug collision is reported rather than silently overwriting the existing profile's decoding rules, so an integrator can carry a tuned deadband from one site to the next without risking a re-point of an in-use profile. The frontend gained a Discovery page and a first-run onboarding wizard that lead with enrollment as the primary onboarding path. mDNS/SSDP/portscan discovery and a Modbus TCP scan, both originally scoped to P3, were deliberately deferred: MQTT sensors announce over MQTT, not mDNS, so a network scan would mostly find gateways rather than sensors, and the Modbus scan belongs with the Modbus poller in P5 where it can be tested against a real device.
compatibility: New app surface only; myiotsan has no prior installs or deployed fleets to migrate. The broker's Authenticator interface signature changed (AuthenticateDevice/AuthorizeTopic now use a Principal struct instead of a bare device id) — an infra/iot/mqtt-internal change with one production implementer (myiotsan's own DeviceService), so no other app is affected. No enrollment window is open by default on boot; the broker's device-table-only admission behavior for existing installs is unchanged unless an admin explicitly opens a window. mymatasan, myidsan and myseliasan are untouched by this change.
